questions.stem: A man takes 10 days to complete a piece of work, while his son takes 15 days to do the same work. If they work together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Let total work be the LCM of 10 and 15, which is 30 units.
Man's efficiency = 30 / 10 = 3 units/day.
Son's efficiency = 30 / 15 = 2 units/day.
Combined efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day.
Time taken together = Total Work / Combined Efficiency = 30 / 5 = 6 days.
DECOY BUSTING: The most common trap is just averaging the days: (10+15)/2 = 12.5 days. Working together always takes LESS time than the fastest worker.
EXAM INSIGHT: A quick formula for two people working together is (A * B) / (A + B). Here: (10 * 15) / (10 + 15) = 150 / 25 = 6 days.
